# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (compact reference)

## BOOK 1 of 2: THE BOYS OF GRAND PRÉ SCHOOL (James De Mille, Gutenberg 56232)
Series: "B. O. W. C." Lee & Shepard, Boston. Chapters I–XXIII, no XXIV heading (XXIV appears as final chapter).

**Main characters**
- Boys of the "B. O. W. C." secret society: **Bart** (leader, imaginative, quick at rhymes; Bart Rawdon), **Bruce Rawdon** (Bart's older brother; strong, brave, secretly superstitious about ghosts; leads Scott's Bay party in ch. XIV), **Arthur** (Bruce/Bart's brother, Rawdons), **Phil**, **Tom**.
- **Solomon**: aged African-American servant, "Grand Panjandrum" of the B.O.W.C.; dialect speech; cook of Academy, "cool an' airy 'partment"; terrified by ghost noises; calls himself "Gasperojum".
- **Captain Corbet**: meek, venerable, dialect-speaking former sea captain, owns schooner **Antelope** (carries potatoes); devoted to infant "babby" (his baby); wife **Mrs. Corbet** (away visiting relatives, high-spirited); owns a "mineral rod" bought from old Zeke, a demon in human form.
- **Mr. Long**: teacher, eloquent, leonine, defends Corbet at trial. **Dr. Porter**: headmaster, antiquarian, Museum curator. **Mr. Simmons**: teacher, mineralogy.
- **Pat**: Irish servant/student, mischievous; lives in attic room; hoaxer of garret noises (with string to bell, knocks, owl); lost in woods chasing porcupine (calls it "wild turkey", "wild duck", "goose with four legs").
- **Jiggins, Bogud, Billymack, Johnny Blue, Muckle, Sammy Ram Ram, David Digg**: other boys.
- **Captain Pratt**: jovial potato-freight captain who raises the Antelope.
- **Old Zeke**: worthless witness at trial ("Old Zeke's rat").
- **Pieter Schwab**: Dutch-descended justice of peace ("Rhadamanthus").
- **Benedict Bellefontaine**: wealthiest Acadian farmer of Grand Pré (legend).
- **Gaspereaugians**: rival boys of Gaspereau valley; their big leader wrestled by Bruce.

**Events in order**
- Ch I: Spring recess ends. Camp in woods (dam, pool, camp of fir). Solomon's lunch. Captain Corbet arrives; shows "mineral rod" and copper coin (LOUIS XIV. ROI DE FRANCE). Says pot of gold buried in "Old French Orchard" behind Academy; rod dipped at one cellar.
- Ch II: View from hill (Blomidon, Minas Basin, Cornwallis, Horton Bluff, Five Islands). History of Acadian banishment (Evangeline reference). Corbet's rod falls at cellar centre. Boys decide to dig at midnight, secret, with magic rules (lights in multiples of 3 or 7, silence).
- Ch III: Midnight dig, 21 lights in pails/kettles, Bust (statue) as palladium. Chant in Latin/History/Euclid; hymn to "Rousseau's Dream". Bruce strikes metal. Terrifying roar; panic; all flee (Solomon first, Corbet "O, my babby!"). Bruce returns first; they refill hole.
- Ch IV: Sunrise description. Mr. Long asks boys to unload Antelope's ballast (stone wall from Mud Creek farm owner) and rebuild it; reward: holidays. Antelope capsizes in Mud Creek on falling tide. Corbet says "gone sucker," "finger of Providence". Corbet served writ over stone wall; Mr. Long promises to defend.
- Ch V: Garret noises (howls, knocks) in Academy attic; Pat suspected. Bart explores alone later, keeps findings secret.
- Ch VI: Trial at Pieter Schwab's hall; claim $500 damages; Old Zeke's rat; Mr. Long wins; Corbet hero; "apotheosis" of baby.
- Ch VII: Gaspereaux valley; Bruce's party fishes and visits bridge; find Gaspereaugians at camp.
- Ch VIII: Bart and Solomon captured by ambush; Bart jests; slips bonds; Bruce defeats big Gaspereaugian wrestler (dumps him in pool). Escape; basket recovered. "Exeunt omnes Gaspereaugienses!"
- Ch IX: Picnic at cellar; roar heard again; donkey (Dr. Porter's, "Neddy") brays — mystery solved. Solomon's laughter. Boys decide to dig again in daylight.
- Ch X: Dig: ironwork discovered = ploughshare (rusty). Also colter, bolts, ox chain, iron pot, nails, 13 copper "UN SOU" coins, horse/cow bone. Presented to Dr. Porter, who laughs.
- Ch XI: Dr. Porter's proposal: excursion to Blomidon / French fort by wagon with morning start. Explanation of Acadian expulsion (Halifax 1749; Governor; Braddock; ships chartered from Boston "Messrs. Apthorp & Hancock").
- Ch XII (ch XII/XIII): Drive via Cornwallis, North Mountain; breakfast; Dr. Porter's history speech. Walk into primeval forest; Barrens; fog; boys lost.
- Ch XIII–XIV: Reach cliff with surf; party splits: Bruce (Scott's Bay party: Bart, Arthur, Tom, Phil, Pat) vs Doctor (Jiggins, Bogud, Sammy, Johnny, Billymack). Pat chases porcupine, lost, found on road.
- Ch XV–XVI: Bruce & Pat's party and doctor's party reunite at night on road; doctor swerved left; they reach Scott's Bay, cottage of **Bennie Grigg** (Mrs. Bennie); massive spread of food; sleep on hay; Sunday; Monday walk back to horses; return on Monday ~11 a.m. (school had been delayed; extra holiday).
- Ch XVII–XVIII: Garret hoax by Pat with string to bell, knock, donkey hauled up via stairs with carpets; Pat hides; donkey brays; Pat flees. Solomon's supper; Jiggins superstitious.
- Ch XIX–XX: Mr. Long's study: wigging; Pat confesses; owl (Mr. Slocum's escaped screech owl); Captain Corbet arrives with baby; Mr. Long leaves hurriedly. Relics placed in Museum; Bart's poem "True Theory of the Bone".
- Ch XXI–XXII: Lecture on Acadians; Louisbourg first siege (Pepperell, 1745; Vaughn, Royal Battery). School Monday. Boys visit wharf; Antelope still in mud.
- Ch XXIII: Captain Pratt raises Antelope (crew list; "Hi ho, cheerly, men!"); boys summon Corbet by Pat (who minds baby, fails). Corbet's emotional farewell, sails on Antelope with potatoes to Boston, mate Wade; disappears into fog bank.

## BOOK 2 of 2: DOROTHY (Evelyn Raymond, Gutenberg 40300; Hurst & Co., 1907)
Chapters I–XVIII.

**Main characters**
- **Dorothy C.** (Dorothy Chester): foundling, ~12-13 years old, brown eyes, yellow/brown curly hair, bright, impulsive, vain of small feet; calls adoptive mother "mother Martha"; father "father John"; note pinned: "My name is Dorothy C. I have come to be your daughter"; note in misspelled hand: "thee child Is wun Yere an too Munths old hur burthDay is aPrill Furst... Ten doLurs" signed "dorothy's Gardeen hur X mark".
- **John Chester**: postman, "Johnnie" to Mrs. Cecil, whistling postman; later diagnosed locomotor ataxia; sent to hospital, then country, Hudson highlands farm (rock hill-farm willed by uncle to Martha).
- **Martha Chester**: tidy housewife, "Mrs. John Chester", adoptive mother.
- **Mrs. Cecil Somerset Calvert** ("Miss Betty"): proud old Maryland dame, Bellevieu mansion (eagle-gate, two Great Dane dogs Peter and Ponce); servants **Ephraim** (coachman, half-deaf), **Dinah** (ancient maid, dialect), **Methuselah Bonaparte Washington "Brown"** (small boy), cook. Summer home: Deerhurst in Hudson highlands; later Skyrie (Dorothy's new home).
- **Mabel Bruce**: plumber's daughter, chum, always hungry; parents Mr. and Mrs. Bruce (plumber, Bill); Mrs. Jones (Jane), sister-in-law to Mrs. Bruce, takes No. 77 as tenant at $20/mo; husband Bill Jones, night watchman.
- **Miss Georgia**: vice-principal teacher.
- **Mr. Lathrop**: postman friend who helps Dorothy at post office; leaves with Chesters as escort; detective.
- **Mr. Smith** ("John Smith", lawyer on Howard Street): kidnapper; sends Dorothy to hospital; drugs; holds her in Howard Street flat; surname later "Kidder" firm; real identity: former clerk of Kidder & Kidder. Witness-threat plotting. Later sick with measles, dies/is arrested.
- **Miranda Stott** ("Mrs. Denim"): truck farmer, harsh, obeys son ("him"), Smith is her son (sick with measles). Tiger: mastiff.
- **Jim Barlow**: orphan farm-boy, tall, thin, white-haired, bare feet, learning to read ("Baker", "Tinker"); later sent to Deerhurst as gardener.
- **Daniel St. John**: elderly preacher with green goggles, gig, horse Nan; kind Good Samaritan; hymns "Bringing in the sheaves", "Throw out the life line".
- **Aunt Chloe Chester**: old aunt who raised John.

**Events in order**
- Ch I: Spring morning, Martha finds baby in wicker wagon on marble step; postman John Chester; note; Mrs. Cecil stops John; baby 'Dorothy C.' spills milk; Martha decides to keep her ("she's mine").
- Ch II: Dorothy (12/13) scrubs steps, Friday; John tells: "I am doomed" — ataxia; Mrs. Cecil at Bellevieu; dogs knock Dorothy down; Mrs. Cecil says John breaking law; Dorothy missing.
- Ch III: House empty, neighbor says John taken to Johns Hopkins; Dorothy runs barefoot in storm; colored boy's misdirection; "Christ the Healer" statue; faints; nurse. Martha arrives.
- Ch IV: John has a chance of recovery; Dorothy buys white shoes ($1.97) with ten dollars saved; toe hurts; stranger (Mr. Smith) on steps offers "great fortune".
- Ch V: Sunday; Dorothy entertains Mabel; eats ham; tells of moving; Mabel leaves; Smith returns; Dorothy sends Mabel home.
- Ch VI: Dorothy's errand plans; Martha explains country property (hill-farm in Hudson highlands); Dorothy goes to post office Monday.
- Ch VII: At post office, Mr. Lathrop helps; Dorothy asks postmaster to take father's place; Smith catches her, takes her to Howard Street flat; writes note; envelope with money enclosed.
- Ch VIII: Martha frantic; Mrs. Bruce & Mrs. Jones (tenant); rent $20; Mr. Lathrop; John depressed; photograph of Dorothy.
- Ch IX: Dorothy locked in Howard Street flat; Smith returns; hack-driver; milk drugged; she wakes at farm; note "Drink no milk."
- Ch X: Detective; Mabel questioned ("Tall. Light hair. Left eye squints. Eyebrows meet. Glib."); flitting Wed; John refuses to go without Dorothy; newspaper headline: "KIDNAPPING AND MURDER THE PROBABLE SOLUTION."
- Ch XI: Dorothy at Stott farm; strawberries; Jim Barlow reveals "powders" in milk; plan to escape.
- Ch XII: Measles caught; Miranda nurses her; Dorothy and Jim learn spelling (Baker, Tinker); Smith sick upstairs, dying.
- Ch XIII: Mrs. Cecil and plumber Mr. Bruce; "$100 reward" then "five hundred dollars" advertisement; Kidder & Kidder lawyers.
- Ch XIV: Jim learns of $500 reward in newspaper; Dorothy plans escape; Smith kept in attic; Miranda locks her in harness room.
- Ch XV: Flight at night; cross-lots; Dorothy steps on thorn; faints; Jim carries her; "Pshaw!".
- Ch XVI: Dorothy prays; Daniel St. John finds them under honeysuckle hedge; breakfast at his cottage; Sunday.
- Ch XVII: Mrs. Cecil's Sunday drive; sees fox-hunt; rescues Dorothy and Jim; takes them to Bellevieu; Dorothy's ailing foot.
- Ch XVIII: Conclusion: Kidder explains Smith was former clerk; Mrs. Cecil to take Dorothy to Skyrie; reunion with John & Martha; Jim to Deerhurst; "THE END".
